title: Build your own monorepo
items: A new monorepo kit lets you choose web, API, docs and mobile frameworks, with libraries and tools configured separately for each service.
The eight existing monorepo presets now share the same configurator. Workspace tasks can use simple scripts, Turborepo or Nx.
Generated projects include web-to-API connection settings, CI for each service and deployment instructions. Requires CLI 1.1.0 or newer.

title: A fuller catalog for every stack, and one Security pack
items: The shared catalog now has 256 entries, with 144 new library, tooling and deployment options across TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, C#, Ruby, PHP, Java, Kotlin, Swift and Dart.

All 70 official kits were reviewed for compatible categories. Nuxt now offers Vercel, Netlify, Docker and Railway, plus auth, database, payments, email, i18n, observability and testing choices. SvelteKit gets its own Vercel, Netlify and Node adapters.

Expanded native and backend choices include Flutter state/data packages, Swift Package Manager integrations, Android libraries, Rust crates, ASP.NET Core packages, Spring starters and official server SDKs. Setup tasks identify configuration that still needs to be completed.

Deployment choices follow the project platform: browser and VS Code extensions get their publishing destinations, desktop apps get release distribution, and monorepos keep deployment and dependencies scoped to their services.
Every catalog entry now has an icon: a publisher mark when available, otherwise a semantic icon for its category, in both themes.

One general Security pack with 12 skills replaces the separate AI security add-on. It covers code, auth, access control, web/APIs, mobile, infrastructure, secrets and dependencies; LLM/MCP checks apply when the project implements those features.

create-first-commit 1.0.3 adds platform-aware catalog compatibility and improves verification: project build combinations exclude skills, while skill names are checked separately from their official source files with an installer fallback.
A generated coverage report documents the options offered by each kit. New verification matrix entries exercise the added catalog choices without requiring production credentials.
Design, Security and first-commit skill packs start compact. Expand each pack to inspect and select its skills; inclusion switches remain available independently.

title: first-commit is live
items: Launch day: first-commit.dev is open, and create-first-commit 1.0.0 is the first stable release of the CLI on npm.
One command takes an empty folder to a first commit: the framework's official setup, the libraries you pick, skills and MCP servers for your agent, and an AGENTS.md written for your stack.
70 official kits to start from (landing pages, web apps, SaaS, APIs, mobile apps, monorepos and extensions), each tested in CI on Linux and macOS.
A shared catalog of 100+ libraries (UI, auth, databases, payments, email, AI, observability, testing and deployment) you can add to any kit from the configurator.
Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf and OpenCode. Free, with no account needed to create a project.
